title: Multi-Tab Wallet Checkout Balance Debit Race Condition
businessContext: A digital wallet and subscription checkout interface allows users to redeem promo gift balances. When a user opens multiple browser tabs or clicks "Pay with Balance" concurrently, two requests race against each other, allowing the user to spend a $50 balance twice.
problemStatement: Design a client-side and API concurrency guard. On the client side, implement an asynchronous mutex / queue runner that prevents parallel in-flight checkout mutations for the same wallet ID, serializes requests, and handles cancellation / idempotency headers.
constraints: Must guarantee only 1 mutation per key runs at any time.
Pending invocations should queue or reject cleanly with ConcurrentOperationError.
Must clean up queue state when promises resolve or reject to avoid memory leaks.
candidateTasks: Implement `runExclusive(key, task)` using Promise chaining or a queue of resolvers.
Ensure if `task()` throws an exception, the next queued task still executes and the error is propagated to the caller.
Delete the lock from `this.locks` when the queue for that key becomes empty.
hints: Track a current Promise for each key: `this.locks.get(key) || Promise.resolve()`.
Chain the next task onto that promise using `.finally()`.
Be careful to catch errors in the chain so a failure does not block subsequent tasks in the queue forever.

testCases.name: Serializes tasks sequentially for same key
testCases.explanation: Task 2 must wait until Task 1 finishes completely before starting.

alternativeApproaches: FIFO Array queue of defer resolvers with an active worker loop.
Distributed Redis Redlock / optimistic concurrency token on the server side (crucial for multi-server setups).
commonMistakes: Using a simple boolean flag: between the check and the async operation, another invocation enters.
Uncaught exceptions in task 1 causing task 2 to hang forever because release() is not in a finally block.
